items.title: Daniel in the Lions’ Den
items.summary: Daniel's faithfulness earns him responsibility, but jealous officials exploit a royal decree to trap him. Daniel continues his regular prayer, is thrown into the lions' den, and is preserved. The king later acknowledges the living God who rescues Daniel.
items.lesson: Integrity is built through ordinary habits long before a public test comes. Be faithful, pray steadily, and stand for what is right without seeking conflict.
items.prayer: God of Daniel, strengthen my integrity, deepen my prayer, and help me act faithfully under pressure.

items.title: The Three Young Men in the Furnace
items.summary: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego refuse to worship the king's image. They trust God even when they cannot predict the outcome, and the king sees them preserved in the furnace. Their witness challenges the demand to place political power above God.
items.lesson: Faithfulness is not a bargain in which we demand a particular outcome from God. It is loyalty to God and conscience even when the future is uncertain.
items.prayer: Lord, give me courage to keep my conscience clear and respect those whose beliefs differ from mine.

items.title: Nehemiah Rebuilds the Walls
items.summary: When Nehemiah hears that Jerusalem's walls lie broken, he prays, plans, seeks permission and organises people for the work. Opposition and discouragement do not end the effort; the community rebuilds by working together.
items.lesson: Prayer and planning belong together. Lasting repair needs practical effort, shared responsibility and persistence.
items.prayer: God of restoration, help me turn concern into wise action and work patiently with others.

items.title: The Valley of Dry Bones
items.summary: Ezekiel sees a valley filled with dry bones, an image of a people who have lost hope. At God's word, the bones are joined and receive life. The vision promises restoration to a community that thinks its future has ended.
items.lesson: When a community feels exhausted, small signs of solidarity and renewal matter. Hope can begin before the whole situation is repaired.
items.prayer: God of life, breathe hope into weary hearts and teach me to help rebuild what has been broken.

items.title: The Wisdom of Job
items.summary: Job suffers losses that he cannot explain. His friends offer confident answers that fail to honour his pain. God eventually speaks from the whirlwind, and Job encounters a mystery far greater than easy explanations. The book refuses to reduce suffering to a simple formula.
items.lesson: Do not blame people for their suffering or pretend every hardship has an easy explanation. Faith can include honest lament, questions and companionship.
items.prayer: God of compassion, help me accompany people who suffer without offering shallow answers.

items.title: The Beatitudes
items.summary: Jesus teaches on the mountain and calls blessed those who are poor in spirit, meek, merciful, pure in heart, peacemakers and persecuted for righteousness. His vision reverses the world's usual measurements of status and success.
items.lesson: Holiness is revealed in mercy, justice, peacemaking and fidelity—not in popularity or power.
items.prayer: Jesus, form my heart according to the Beatitudes and help me make peace where I live and work.

items.title: The Lord’s Prayer
items.summary: When the disciples ask Jesus to teach them to pray, he gives them a prayer centred on the Father's name, God's Kingdom, daily bread, forgiveness and deliverance from evil. Prayer becomes a way of ordering life around God's will and our dependence on one another.
items.lesson: Prayer is more than asking for things. It teaches trust, daily responsibility and the difficult work of forgiving others.
items.prayer: Father, let Your Kingdom shape my choices; give us what we need and make us people of forgiveness.

items.title: The Parable of the Talents
items.summary: A master entrusts resources to servants before travelling. Two servants put what they receive to work, while another hides it in fear. Jesus challenges disciples to be responsible with the gifts and opportunities entrusted to them.
items.lesson: Faithfulness means using time, ability and opportunity responsibly, rather than letting fear prevent every good action.
items.prayer: Lord, show me how to use my gifts wisely for the good of others.

items.title: Zacchaeus Makes Restitution
items.summary: Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector, climbs a tree to see Jesus. Jesus calls him down and chooses to stay at his house. The encounter leads Zacchaeus to give to the poor and repay those he has defrauded, showing that welcome can begin a concrete change of life.
items.lesson: Conversion is not only a feeling. It includes repairing harm, making restitution where possible and changing unfair practices.
items.prayer: Jesus, welcome me into Your mercy and give me courage to make right what I have done wrong.

items.title: The Woman at the Well
items.summary: Jesus speaks with a Samaritan woman at a well, crossing social and religious boundaries. Their conversation moves from ordinary water to living water, and she returns to her town to tell others about the encounter.
items.lesson: Respectful conversation can open a path to understanding. No one should be reduced to a stereotype or excluded from a sincere encounter.
items.prayer: Lord Jesus, teach me to listen without prejudice and to share hope with humility.

items.title: The Healing of Bartimaeus
items.summary: Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, cries out to Jesus while the crowd tries to silence him. Jesus stops, asks what he wants, and restores his sight. The crowd must learn that the person they tried to quiet deserves to be heard.
items.lesson: Listen to people whose voices are dismissed. Ask what help they want instead of deciding for them without listening.
items.prayer: Jesus, open my eyes to the dignity and needs of people others overlook.

items.title: The Forgiving Father and the Older Brother
items.summary: In Jesus' parable, a father welcomes home a returning son, while the older brother resents the celebration. The father goes out to both sons, showing that mercy seeks restoration and also addresses the pain of those who feel overlooked.
items.lesson: Mercy invites everyone into reconciliation. Honest hurt should be heard, but resentment need not have the final word.
items.prayer: Father, help me receive mercy, speak honestly about hurt, and rejoice when others begin again.

items.title: Jesus and the Children
items.summary: People bring children to Jesus, but the disciples try to stop them. Jesus rebukes the disciples, welcomes the children and blesses them. His action challenges communities that put barriers between vulnerable people and care.
items.lesson: A community shaped by Jesus makes room for children and protects the dignity of those with less power.
items.prayer: Jesus, make my community welcoming, safe and attentive to every child.

items.title: The Road to Damascus
items.summary: Saul travels to persecute Christians when a light and a voice confront him. Blinded, he must depend on others; Ananias approaches him despite fear, prays for him and helps him begin a new life. The persecutor becomes a witness to Christ.
items.lesson: Real conversion changes how we treat people. It may require humility, help from others and the courage to repair our direction.
items.prayer: Lord, correct my path when I am wrong and help me welcome the possibility of change in others.

items.title: Peter and Cornelius
items.summary: Peter receives a vision that challenges his assumptions about purity and inclusion. When he meets Cornelius and his household, the Holy Spirit is poured out on Gentiles too. Peter recognises that God shows no partiality.
items.lesson: Let God challenge prejudice. The Church must recognise the dignity of people beyond familiar cultural and social boundaries.
items.prayer: Holy Spirit, reveal my hidden prejudices and help me welcome others with justice and humility.

items.title: The Early Church Shares Its Goods
items.summary: The first believers devote themselves to the apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread and prayer. They share resources so that people in need are cared for. Their common life makes the Gospel visible in practical solidarity.
items.lesson: Christian fellowship includes material responsibility. Faith communities should notice need and organise help fairly and transparently.
items.prayer: Lord, make our community generous, honest and attentive to people who lack what they need.

items.title: The Armour of God
items.summary: Paul describes truth, righteousness, readiness for peace, faith, salvation and God's word as armour for spiritual struggle. The passage ends with a call to persistent prayer for all the saints.
items.lesson: Spiritual strength is not permission to attack people. It means standing firm in truth, justice, peace and prayer.
items.prayer: God, clothe me with truth and justice, make me ready to bring peace, and keep me faithful in prayer.

items.title: Love in First Corinthians
items.summary: Paul places love at the centre of Christian gifts and service. Eloquence, knowledge, generosity and sacrifice lose their purpose when they are separated from patience, kindness and truth. Love remains when temporary gifts pass away.
items.lesson: Measure spiritual maturity by patient, truthful love—not attention, talent or impressive words alone.
items.prayer: Lord, purify my intentions and teach me to love in practical, patient ways.

items.title: The New Creation
items.summary: John sees a new heaven and a new earth. God dwells with humanity, wipes away tears and brings an end to death, mourning and pain. The vision gives suffering communities a promise of renewal and calls them to persevere in hope.
items.lesson: Christian hope looks toward God's renewal of creation and encourages us to comfort the grieving and work for what is just now.
items.prayer: God of the new creation, comfort those who mourn and make me a worker for justice and hope.
